correctness.rationale: The Bergman–Laplace isometry Ug(z)=(2pi)^(-1/2)int_0^infinity sqrt(2t)g(t)e^(itz)dt converts horizontal-line mass into the positive multiplier m_beta(t)=2t sum_{j>=0}2^(-beta j)e^(-2t2^(-j)). Setting u=2t and adding negative dyadic indices gives m_beta(u/2)=u^(1-beta){P_beta(log_2 u)-R_beta(u)} with P_beta=sum_{k in Z}2^(beta(k+theta))e^(-2^(k+theta)), R_beta=sum_{k>=1}(2^ku)^beta e^(-2^ku). Mellin substitution yields Fourier coefficients Gamma(beta-2pi i ell/log2)/log2, with rapidly convergent series. Positivity and boundedness of P_beta, and exponential decay of R_beta at infinity, yield boundedness iff beta>=1. At beta=1, the omitted R_1 is positive for all finite u while the completed periodic supremum K is approached along u=2^(n+theta*), so the optimal one-sided and two-sided constants coincide and no nonzero extremizer exists. The exact Gamma modulus bound makes the second and higher harmonic derivative tails <9e-6 of the first, giving exactly one maximum and one minimum per period. Multiplier real analyticity and nonconstancy on nonatomic L2 explain noncompactness, absence of eigenvalues and spectrum [0,norm] for bounded cases. An independent mpmath Mellin and Fourier evaluation agreed to better than 1e-24 and recovered theta*=.8611035250777802693 and K=1.4427093011329494542; numerical agreement supports, but does not replace, the proof.
